Today, we completed our acquisition of Confluent, Inc., the data streaming platform that more than 6,500 enterprises, including 40% of the Fortune 500, rely on to power real-time operations.  Together, we deliver a smart data platform providing every AI model, agent, and automated workflow with the real-time and trusted data to operate across on-premises and hybrid cloud environments at scale.  As enterprises move from AI experimentation to production, the critical barrier to success is the data—clean, governed, continuously refreshed—and delivered at the speed and scale AI demands. However, in most enterprises today, data remains siloed across systems and environments and arrives hours or days after it is generated.  IDC estimates that over a billion new logical applications will emerge by 2028, driven by a new generation of AI that will only deliver value if the data behind it is live, trusted, and continuously flowing. That scale of demand requires a new kind of data foundation, and by acquiring Confluent, we address that challenge directly, giving enterprises a single, governed platform where AI models and agents can operate with context, in real time, across every environment. "Transactions happen in milliseconds, and AI decisions need to happen just as fast. With Confluent, we are giving clients the ability to move trusted data continuously across their entire operation so their AI models and agents can act on what is happening right now, not on data that is hours old." - Rob Thomas, SVP, IBM Software and Chief Commercial Officer IBM and Confluent Product Synergies  Today’s announcement brings immediate integrations across our software portfolio, including: AI-Ready, Real-Time Data 🚀 Enterprise AI technologies need current context, not yesterday’s data. Confluent streams live operational events directly into watsonx․data – ensuring every model, agent, and workflow runs on continuously updated enterprise data, with lineage, policy enforcement, and quality controls included.  Activate the Modernized Mainframe in the AI era 🤖 The most critical business transactions in the world have long run on IBM Z. With IBM Z and Confluent, organizations can identify and drive real-time events at the transaction source as well as stream transactional data directly for real-time analytics, automation, and AI workflows. This enables mission-critical transaction processing to integrate tightly with the rest of the business in real-time, at enterprise scale. Event-Driven Automation Across Hybrid Environments⚡ IBM MQ and IBM webMethods Hybrid Integration form the foundation of enterprise event-driven automation, combining trusted transactional messaging with modern integration and orchestration across hybrid environments. Confluent extends this platform with high-scale event streaming, enabling applications, APIs, and AI agents to sense and act on business events in real time. How Enterprises are Using Confluent, Today Built on Apache Kafka®, the standard for data streaming, Confluent is already embedded in the operational fabric of the world's largest enterprises, with a customer base that spans industries from financial services and healthcare to manufacturing and retail.  🛞 Michelin → relies on Confluent to manage real-time inventory across a supply chain spanning 170 countries — achieving 35% cost savings without sacrificing visibility or control. 💄 L'Oréal → uses Confluent to stream IoT sensor data across its smart factories — turning raw manufacturing signals into real-time quality control and operational decisions at global scale. 🚗 BMW Group → streams IoT data from 30+ production sites and its global sales network in real time, connecting factory floor systems and cloud applications across the organization.  🎟️ Ticketmaster → streams ticket inventory, sales, and customer activity in real time across hundreds of systems, reducing development friction and powering machine learning at scale.  "Since our founding, Confluent’s mission has been to set the world’s data in motion, making data streaming as foundational to the enterprise as the database. Joining IBM allows us to accelerate that mission at a much greater scale. IBM’s global reach and deep enterprise relationships will help us go further, faster. As enterprises move from experimenting with AI to running their business on it, helping data flow continuously across the business has never mattered more. I’m excited to see what we’ll build together.” - Jay Kreps, CEO and Co-founder of Confluent See how Michelin cut costs with Confluent ⤵ What Analysts are Saying With Confluent, IBM Consulting and IBM partners, will help clients build the data foundation their AI needs — live, governed, and continuously flowing across every system and environment. "The shift from AI experimentation to production deployment has exposed a critical gap in enterprise data architecture: the inability to deliver trusted, real-time data to the systems that need it most. AI agents and automated workflows don't operate on historical data — they require live operational signals, continuously flowing across the enterprise as events occur...IBM has methodically assembled a portfolio that addresses both sides of this equation — governance and infrastructure for data at rest, and now a proven, enterprise-grade platform for data in motion. The result is one of the most complete enterprise AI data stacks in the market today. - Sanjeev Mohan, Principal Analyst, SanjMo    The closing of our acquisition of Confluent includes all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Confluent for $31 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of $11 billion.   👉 Learn more in this blog

subject: The deadline has passed, how judging works and give us your feedback! - Amazon Nova AI Hackathon
email_text:
( http://devpost.com )

The submission portal is officially locked.

First and foremost: Thank you. We know it takes a lot of caffeine, late-night debugging, and creative energy to get a project across the finish line. Whether you built a seamless Voice AI experience with Nova 2 Sonic or a complex multi-agent system, you should be incredibly proud of what you’ve shipped!

 

🛑 Project Status & Post-Hackathon Building
---------------------------------------------

To ensure a fair playing field, no more edits can be made to your projects. 

*
Keep your repos "As-Is": Please do not push any new code to the repository linked in your submission.

*
*
Want to keep building? We love the hustle! If you are building your project out beyond the hackathon, please wait until after the winner announcement on April 8th.
*
The Fork Rule: If you can't wait to iterate, please fork your code repository. Continue your masterpiece in the new fork while leaving the original hackathon submission branch untouched so judges see exactly what was submitted.

 

⚖️ The Judging Process: what happens next?
----------------------------------------------

Our panel is diving into your builds as we speak and will be busy reviewing projects until April 2nd. Here is how the evaluation will roll out:

Stage One: Baseline Viability (Pass/Fail)

We first ensure every submission meets the "baseline level of viability." Does it include all requirements? Does it reasonably address a challenge? Does it actually use Amazon Nova?

 

Stage Two: The Deep Dive

Submissions that pass Stage One move to our expert panel for scoring (1–5 scale) based on these weighted criteria:

*
Technical Implementation - 60% Includes the quality, effectiveness, successful integration with Amazon Nova, and overall system architecture.
*
Enterprise or Community Impact - 20% Assesses how the solution delivers business value or creates meaningful benefits for communities.
*
Creativity and Innovation - 20% Includes the novelty of the approach and innovative use of multi-agent systems to solve real-world problems.

Note on Testing: To respect the judges' time, they may prioritize demo videos for evaluation. While they have access to your code, they are not required to live-test every project if the video clearly demonstrates the functionality.

 

🎁 Help Us Improve (And Win $50!)
-----------------------------------

While you’re waiting on the results, we need your help one more time. Your feedback on Amazon Nova models is incredibly valuable to the Amazon team. What did you love? What could be improved?

* Please take a few minutes to complete our feedback survey ( https://amazon-nova.devpost.com/details/feedback-survey ) by tomorrow, March 18th at 5:00 PM PT.
* The 60 most valuable feedback responses will win $50 in cash. Go complete the survey now!

 

💬 Feedback & Community
-------------------------

Due to the volume of submissions, we cannot provide individual feedback, but we encourage you to share your project links in the Devpost Discord ( https://discord.gg/CzUUmc7h44 ) and get feedback from your peers! We will be opening the Project Gallery in a few days so you can see what your fellow builders have created.

 

Rest up, celebrate your hard work, and stay tuned.

As you've probably noticed, FigJam is easy to learn and simple to use. A few basic tricks move ideas forward even faster.

By Abhishek Kumar


By Abhishek Kumar

Hey Golang Engineers 👋 So i've been working on something for a while now and finally its ready to share. I call it the Interview Field Guide for Golang Engineers — Part 1, Version 1 is available now. This is specifically for intermediate and advanced golang engineers — not for complete beginners - u should also read it though. Think of it as a brush-up guide, a FAQ-style refresher that gets straight to the point. no 10-page explanations for a 2-line answer. Here's a taste of whats inside — Q: What is a Go module and what does go.mod do? A module is a collection of Go code that can be shared and reused. go.mod is basically your project's dependency manifest — it lists every external library and the version your project needs. Go reads this file to resolve, download and lock dependencies. Simple as that. Q: What is MVS (Minimal Version Selection) and why does Go use it? MVS is Go's dependency resolution algorithm. When multiple libraries need different versions of the same dependency, Go picks the highest version that was explicitly requested — not the latest one available. This keeps builds deterministic and reproducible. Avoids the classic "dependency hell" by being deliberate rather then greedy. Mental model: "use the newest version someone specifically asked for." Q: What causes cannot use X as X / unknown revision / missing go.sum entry? Error Cause Fix cannot use X as X Duplicate library with different import paths Unify imports or use replace unknown revision Version tag doesn't exist or private repo not accessible Check the tag; check auth missing go.sum entry Lock file is stale Run go mod tidy Q: How does Go's interface system actually work? What makes it unique? Go uses implicit interface satisfaction — a type doesn't need to declare that it implements an interface. If it has all the required methods, it automatically satisfies the interface. This is structural typing, or "duck typing" at compile time. Very powerful once it clicks. Q: Explain the typed nil bug. Why does this even happen? An interface value secretly holds two fields: (type, value). It's only nil when both are nil. Here's the trap most people fall into — The returned value has a type set, so err != nil evaluates to true even though the underlying value is nil. Nasty bug. Fix: Return nil directly, not a typed nil variable. And if your debugging — use: Q: Whats the difference between eface and iface internally? eface iface Used for any (empty interface) Specific interfaces like error, io.Reader Stores type + value method lookup table (itab) + value The itab is how Go figures out which concrete function to call when you invoke a method on an interface. This is the kind of thing most people never dig into — but knowing it changes how you write and read Go code. And theres a LOT more where that came from. The overall guide ( all parts in building ) covers everything from modules and interfaces to goroutines, channels, memory model, context, error handling patterns and more. Questions that actually come up — in interviews, in code reviews, in team discussions. As I build - your comments and feedback matters a lot. - I will cover many complex and most common issues and patterns in simple language - easy to discuss in teams and during interviews. Why bother when you have ChatGPT or Claude? Fair point. But heres the thing — I've already done ( doing ) the heavy lifting. Its curated, its structured, and its DONE FOR YOU things. You dont have to prompt an AI, sift through a wall of text and figure out what matters. This guide gets to the point. Who is this for? Golang engineers prepping for interviews Devs who want to level up their understanding of existing Go codebases People who want to sound sharp in team discussions and design reviews Anyone who wants a quick, reliable refresher without going through the entire Go spec Golang Interviewers want to ask right questions to candidates. - If you are that one - ping me - If sufficient request come - i will work on specific versions for that objective. Pre-interview calls by HR just to gain some vibs. And its FREE for now. Drop a comment, DM me, or react to this post — i'll send it over within 1-3 days once im online. Don't sleep on this one. ****************
This is your jam
****************

Whether you're looking to work better alongside your team or staking a claim as World's Best Collaborator, FigJam is great for so many things.

The world's best teams use FigJam to brainstorm new ideas, diagram thoughts, and make meetings more effective—and more fun!

Show
me the ropes ( https://www.figma.com/file/2qCC9N7DNi8Go5EInS0TnF/FigJam-basics-(Community)?type=whiteboard&node-id=0-1&utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=hero_btn_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Find the what and how ( https://www.figma.com/file/SpnP5psndexdJuf2IWlAoE/Brainstorming-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=brainstorm_img_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

-------------------------
Transform your brainstorm
-------------------------

Looking for a eureka? Start by adding a few basic questions, grab a few (dozen) stickies ( https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500004414322-Sticky-notes-in-FigJam?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=brainstorm_inline_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma ), and discover great ideas with teammates as you go.

Try brainstorming → ( https://www.figma.com/file/SpnP5psndexdJuf2IWlAoE/Brainstorming-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=brainstorm_cta_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

-----------------------
Do it for the (dia)gram
-----------------------

Diagram thoughts, dreams, a new user journey ( https://www.figma.com/file/8FYotKDlDQaKd3ShriJbVq/Customer-Journey-Map/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=diagram_inline_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma ), or an internal process. FigJam helps turn complex problems into easy-to-understand visuals.

Try diagramming → ( https://www.figma.com/file/GGpts9zMtNJJUN8zy57DjY/Flow-Chart-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=diagram_cta_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Visualize your thoughts ( https://www.figma.com/file/GGpts9zMtNJJUN8zy57DjY/Flow-Chart-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=diagram_img_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Share more with your team ( https://www.figma.com/file/4UoBZZyVBizLzzWLjtv7ez/Weekly-Team-Kickoff-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=meetings_cta_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

------------------------
Make meetings meaningful
------------------------

From kickoffs to retros, a productive meeting starts with engagement. Stamps, widgets ( https://www.figma.com/community/category/whiteboarding?resource_type=widgets&utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=meetings_inline_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma ), and one-of-a-kind doodles keep everyone energized.

Kick off a kickoff → ( https://www.figma.com/file/4UoBZZyVBizLzzWLjtv7ez/Weekly-Team-Kickoff-Template/duplicate?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=meetings_cta_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Don't know where to start? Generate a personalized template in seconds—with a little help from AI.

Generate a template ( https://figma.com/jam?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_onb&utm_content=tip_d1&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Try FigJam ( https://figma.com/jam?utm_source=figma&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fj_ob&utm_content=toolbar&utm_campaign=Onboarding+-+FJ+New+User&utm_content=Day+01+-+Welcome+-+FJ+New&utm_medium=email&utm_source=figma )

Show, don’t just tell. Get to the UI/CLI within the first 30 seconds.

It’s okay to use AI for your voiceover to narrate your demo. Rehearse your talking points ahead of time to ensure your 3 minutes are meaningful.
*
Don't forget: Include that #AmazonNova hashtag!

[ ] The Tagline: Does your project name stand out? (Think "Vibrant" vs "Nova-App-V1").

Picking the right model for your task is hard. You have to consider multiple variables, such as speed, price, intelligence, and response quality (vibes).

We believe this is a great place to start and get an understanding of different models. For example, you can test models with or without reasoning, or compare open-source models with proprietary ones.

OpenRouter publishes real-world data about how models are used across different categories ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=ModelDiscovery-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io#categories ), programming languages ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=ModelDiscovery-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io#programming-languages ), tool calls ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=ModelDiscovery-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io#tools ), and image inputs ( https://openrouter.ai/rankings?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=ModelDiscovery-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io#images ).
* Evaluate pricing, latency, and throughput. You can find all this information on every model page. You should spend some time exploring the benefits and trade-offs.

A bonus hint: OpenRouter has presets ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/presets?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=ModelDiscovery-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) that allow you to separate your configuration from your code.

Job Search Tip: Before a recruiter opens your resume, something else already 
has.



At Google, a single role can get 10,000 applications. At a Series B startup, 
it might be 800. Companies are using AI tools to narrow that volume before a 
human ever gets involved—and most candidates have no idea how those tools 
interpret their documents.



Edward Rodriguez 
<https://linkedin.com/in/edwardxrodriguez/?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_feed%3BCNGA0KsIQT6ln%2Fsp%2FE8W7Q%3D%3D>
 has spent 8+ years building teams at companies like Celonis, LeafLink, and 
Rhino. His advice is simpler than you'd expect: paste your resume into ChatGPT 
and ask if it's readable. Use the exact keywords from the job description—not 
synonyms, the actual words. Save it as a clean PDF.



That's it. Test it the same way a screener would, before you hit apply.

)​

​
Most job searches fail before the interview stage.

Because the signal of value never reaches the recruiter clearly.

Think about the typical job search.

You:

• apply to dozens of roles
• tweak your resume slightly
• wait for responses
• repeat the process

But the real question is rarely asked:

Does your resume communicate impact fast enough?

Over the past few months, I’ve been experimenting with resumes
alongside my accelerator students (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/d0uwx849d7s0ho60kpobmhz26wzpxhlh0ve7p/wnhvg2w2aghqnzzm69b7/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
) and analyzing resumes that consistently generate interviews.

A few patterns keep appearing.

None of them are complicated.

But together, they dramatically change how your resume is
interpreted.

I recently made a video on Action-Metric-Result-Tool formula of
resume. Watch it here (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/d0uwx849d7s0ho60kpobmhz26wzpxhlh0ve7p/7qh7h8h9qggd5ktz/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1TazFUMnpZRXZuZw==
).

Let me walk you through a few that matter.

----------------------------------
1. The location perception problem
----------------------------------

Recruiters often prefer local candidates.

Not because remote candidates are worse.

But because relocation introduces uncertainty.

If your resume shows a different city, a recruiter might
immediately think:

“Will this candidate relocate?”
“Will this delay hiring?”
“Is this worth the extra effort?”

Many times they simply move on.

A small adjustment removes that friction.

Instead of listing only your current location, you can include
the target city you are applying to.

Example:

Seattle, WA
Open to relocation

It signals intent and eliminates unnecessary doubt.

--------------------------------------------------
2. Your job title might be invisible to recruiters
--------------------------------------------------

Many companies invent creative titles internally.

Those titles make sense within the company.

But outside, they confuse recruiters and ATS systems.

For example:

Growth Ninja
Innovation Catalyst
Customer Happiness Hero

These titles may never appear in recruiter searches.

A better approach is to translate the title while keeping it
honest.

Example:

Customer Happiness Hero (Customer Success Manager)

This keeps your internal title accurate while ensuring your
resume appears in relevant searches.

-------------------------------------------------------
3. Bullet points should show impact, not responsibility
-------------------------------------------------------

A common mistake in resumes is describing tasks instead of
outcomes.

Example:

Responsible for social media campaigns
Versus:
Increased Instagram engagement by 145% by implementing a
data-driven content strategy.

The second statement answers three questions immediately:

What changed
How much it changed
What you did to cause it

One simple structure helps enforce this clarity:

Result → Metric → Action

Example:

Reduced customer onboarding time by 40% by redesigning the
onboarding workflow and automating documentation.

The difference seems small, but recruiters read these signals
instantly.

------------------------------------
4. Speak both human and ATS language
------------------------------------

Applicant tracking systems are inconsistent.

Some search for abbreviations.

Others search for full terms.

For example:

SEO vs Search Engine Optimization
CRM vs Customer Relationship Management

A simple way to avoid being filtered incorrectly is to include
both.

Example:

Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
Customer Relationship Management (CRM)

This ensures your resume appears regardless of how the search is
performed.

-----------------------------------------
5. Study people who already have the role
-----------------------------------------

One strategy many strong candidates use (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/d0uwx849d7s0ho60kpobmhz26wzpxhlh0ve7p/wnhvg2w2aghqnzzm69b7/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
)is reverse engineering the language of the role.

Instead of guessing what recruiters want to see, they study the
resumes and LinkedIn profiles of people already working in the
target role.

Patterns quickly emerge.

You start noticing:

• common tools mentioned
• repeated action verbs
• typical metrics used to measure success

This isn't copying.

It's learning how the industry communicates impact.

-------------------------------------
6. Numbers make your resume memorable
-------------------------------------

Human brains process numbers faster than sentences.

When a recruiter sees numbers, they immediately understand scale.

Compare these two examples:

Improved reporting process
Versus
Reduced report generation time from 4 hours to 25 minutes through
automation

The second one instantly communicates value.

Even small numbers help.

Team size.
Projects delivered.
Revenue influenced.
Time saved.

Numbers convert statements into evidence.

-----------------------------
One perspective I often share
-----------------------------

A resume is not a biography.

It is a signal document.

Its only purpose is to answer one question:

Should we interview this person?

When you approach resume writing from that perspective, you start
focusing less on listing everything you've done and more on
communicating the impact clearly.

And that shift often changes the outcome of a job search.

If you want help applying these strategies to your own job
search, that’s exactly what we work on inside my Job Hunting
Accelerator. (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/d0uwx849d7s0ho60kpobmhz26wzpxhlh0ve7p/e0hph7h76xxmo9b8/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
)​
We break down resumes, networking, and interview preparation step
by step with a community of international students going through
the same journey.

The Hot Mess

By Aastha Verma


By Aastha Verma

    
    
    Read this article on LinkedIn to join the conversation
Read on LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/what-i-realised-after-speaking-nit-raipur-aastha-verma-teygf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Ba%2B1dhvd7QjC2SmdvR5AnKQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQEIM4HzHiyK2w&midSig=2mH_BGDnFd-I81&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-ghmp60~mmnexfn1~ye-null-null&eid=ghmp60-mmnexfn1-ye
  
Young minds are brilliant… but sometimes dangerously impatient. Last month I was invited by the Entrepreneurship Cell, NIT Raipur at the National Institute of Technology Raipur to speak on Design Thinking, Critical Thinking and Innovation Design. Standing in that room full of students was an experience I’m still processing. Not because they were silent. Not because they were distracted. Actually the opposite. They were curious. Restless. Hungry. And honestly, that curiosity is the most powerful thing a country can have. But here’s the harsh truth I also noticed. A lot of young founders want the outcome of entrepreneurship without respecting the process of thinking. And that is dangerous. The curiosity is real… but the patience is missing During the Q&A, a student asked me something like: "How do I build a startup that becomes a unicorn quickly?" I paused. Because the question itself reveals the biggest mistake. The goal is not “unicorn.” The goal is “problem.” The biggest companies in the world didn’t start by chasing valuation. They started by solving a very real, very boring problem. Take Mark Zuckerberg When he started Facebook Meta , he wasn’t trying to build a trillion-dollar company. He was trying to solve a simple problem: people in universities wanted a digital identity and connection network. He was 19!!!!! Or look at Brian Chesky, the co-founder of Airbnb . The company started because he couldn’t afford rent. So he rented air mattresses in his apartment to strangers. That tiny hack became a global hospitality platform. In India, Ritesh Agarwal built OYO at just 19 because he noticed something very simple: Budget hotels in India were chaotic and inconsistent. No big vision statement. Just a problem. The real problem with young entrepreneurs Let me say something that may sound blunt. Many young founders today are obsessed with the idea of being a founder. Not obsessed with building something meaningful. They want: • Funding • LinkedIn headlines • Startup conferences • Instagram reels about “hustle” But they skip the most uncomfortable part: thinking deeply about the problem. Design thinking is not a fancy framework for presentations. It is a discipline of humility. It forces you to accept: You may not understand the user yet. And that is hard for ambitious people. Another mistake I see everywhere Students often come with startup ideas like: “An app that connects X with Y.” Or “Uber but for something else.” That is not innovation. That is pattern copying. Real innovation happens when you ask uncomfortable questions like: • Why does this system exist this way? • Why is the customer tolerating this pain? • What assumption is everyone accepting without questioning? Critical thinking is uncomfortable because it forces you to challenge your own ideas first. But here’s the hopeful part Despite all these mistakes… I walked out of that session feeling incredibly optimistic. Because the energy in that room was real. I met students who: • were building side projects • were experimenting with AI tools • were questioning traditional career paths • were not afraid to fail publicly And that courage matters. In fact, most successful founders started with experiments that looked silly at first. Even Airbnb sounded ridiculous in the beginning. “People will sleep in strangers’ houses?” Today millions do. What I told the students before leaving I ended the session with something I deeply believe. If you want to build something meaningful: Obsess over problems, not startups. Talk to users more than investors. Prototype faster than you plan. Question your own assumptions ruthlessly. And most importantly: Don’t rush greatness. The internet has made success look instant. But behind every “overnight success” there are years of invisible thinking. A small personal note As someone who started building companies young myself, I saw a lot of my younger self in that room. The same impatience. The same ambition. The same desire to build something big. And if even a few of those students leave with this realisation, that thinking deeply is the real superpower, then that session was worth every minute. To the students of National Institute of Technology Raipur: Keep asking questions. Just make sure the questions are bigger than the hype. Because the world doesn’t need more startups. It needs better thinkers.

subject: How does OpenRouter pricing work?
email_text:
OpenRouter

OpenRouter ( https://openrouter.ai/?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Pricing-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

Hi Nandini,

You can buy OpenRouter Platform Credits ( https://openrouter.ai/settings/credits?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Pricing-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) and use them for all available models.

The providers determine the model prices, and we never mark them up. There is a flat fee of 5.5% (minimum $ 0.80) when purchasing credits. 

You can bring your own keys (BYOK) from any provider ( https://openrouter.ai/settings/integrations?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Pricing-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) and use them in OpenRouter. The first one million requests per month are always free. After that, we charge 5% for each subsequent request.

Your one million free requests
reset every month. 

If you are an enterprise that requires SSO, SLAs, and committed contracts, please reach out to us ( https://openrouter.ai/enterprise?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Pricing-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ). We can discuss our enterprise offerings and pricing over a call.

Please let us know if you have any questions regarding pricing ( https://openrouter.ai/pricing?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Pricing-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ).

Best,
OpenRouter Team

Dear Customer, 

Fraudsters may offer quick cash, fake jobs, gaming rewards, or online friendships and ask you to receive or transfer money  through your bank account. By agreeing, you may unknowingly become part of a fraud. 
	
	
	
	

To protect yourself from becoming a victim of money mule fraud, follow these tips: 
	
	
	
	

	
	

Avoid: 

Job, quick-income, gaming, or online friendship offers that ask you to receive or transfer money through your bank account. 
	
	
	
	

	
	

Verify: 
The identity and credentials of anyone offering work, rewards, or financial benefits before engaging. 
	
	
	
	

	
	

Use Only For Yourself: 
Your bank account should be used only for your own transactions never for unknown people or sources. 
	
	
	
	

	
	

Never Share:

Launch your career in the rapidly expanding quantum field.

Graduate School of Arts & Sciences



Dear Nandini


The quantum revolution is here, and Boston University is preparing the leaders who will shape it.


BU’s brand-new MS in Quantum Science & Engineering is a one-year, STEM-designated program built to launch you into high-demand roles in quantum computing, quantum hardware development, photonics, and more. The curriculum incorporates expertise across multiple colleges and departments, delivering one of the most comprehensive quantum education experiences available.


Jobs in the quantum workforce are projected to grow 7.7% over the next decade–nearly twice the national average–with an estimated 44,300 annual openings. Boston University aims to equip graduates with the skills needed to succeed in the workforce and to drive innovation in the quantum industry.


Beyond a strong foundation in quantum theory, you’ll gain hands-on experience building real quantum computers and devices in our new, dedicated quantum lab—an opportunity few programs can offer.

email_text:
OpenRouter

OpenRouter ( https://openrouter.ai/?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

Hi Nandini,

OpenRouter never logs your prompts or responses by default.
-----------------------------------------------------------

We only store metadata to keep your service running smoothly:

* Token counts and latency for billing
* Performance metrics for uptime optimization
* Generation activity you can access anytime

You control exactly where your data ( https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) goes.

Each provider has their own data retention and training policies, and you can check a straightforward summary here ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/privacy-logging?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io#data-retention--logging ). 

By default, your paid requests never route to providers that train on your data. You can customize this further by:

* Setting data policies per request in your API calls
* Configuring account-wide settings in your privacy dashboard ( https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )
* Enabling Zero Data Retention (ZDR ( https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/zdr?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )) for enterprise-grade privacy ( https://openrouter.ai/enterprise?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

Want to support model improvements? You may opt into prompt logging for a 1% usage discount ( https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy?utm_campaign=Welcome+Email+Campaign+%232&utm_content=Logging-email&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ), but that's entirely your choice.

Best,
OpenRouter Team

Providers have outages. It's just the nature of the business.

A quick announcement...

​Free Webinar: What to do If you can’t get an H-1B visa (

-----------------------------------------------------------------

Right now I’m hearing the same concern from a lot of tech
professionals.

* Some are trying their luck in this year’s H-1B lottery.
* Some have H-1Bs that may expire in the coming years.
* Others are simply looking for a more predictable long-term
path.

To help break down what options exist now, we are hosting a live
webinar with MobSquad (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/gkuk5de0rqf5hl9kkrxhrh8e3wm7dhmh90k6e/wnh2hghqnl3w95i7/aHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9tb2JzcXVhZA==
) on March 19.

​

We will cover:

* How the Canadian work permit pathway works for tech
professionals
* What timelines actually look like
* How some professionals continue working with U.S. companies
from Canada
* What long-term permanent residency pathways look like

-->Register for FREE Webinar (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/gkuk5de0rqf5hl9kkrxhrh8e3wm7dhmh90k6e/n2hohvhvmlknddt6/aHR0cHM6Ly9sdW1hLmNvbS81dzR5MGhnNw==
)
Register for FREE Webinar ( https://luma.com/5w4y0hg7 )
​
Today’s newsletter is a little different.

Just a small personal note.

A few weeks ago, Kaitlyn and I moved into a new house in North
Carolina.

Six bedrooms. A massive backyard.

The kind of space where you walk in and instinctively look around
like… “Wait, this is actually ours?”

When we first stepped inside, Kaitlyn literally started jumping.
I just stood there quietly for a moment.

And the first image that flashed in my head was not this house.

It was the Kandivali local train in Mumbai.

Packed crowds.
Long commutes.
Sweaty evenings after class.

Then another memory came.

$1.00 tacos.

When I first moved to the U.S. as an international student, that
was one of the cheapest meals I could find.

You start doing little calculations in your head.

If I spend $5 today, that’s $5 less for groceries later.

So you make tradeoffs.

Not dramatic ones.

Just quiet ones that nobody really sees.

You say no to trips your friends are taking.

You skip buying things you kind of want.

You choose the cheaper room in the apartment.

You work during the day.

You build something at night.

For me that “something” slowly became YouTube.

And honestly, for a long time it didn’t look like it was going
anywhere.

There were years where I felt stuck.

Friends moved to bigger cities.

Some landed big tech roles.

Meanwhile I was in Chico, wondering if I had made the right
decisions.

Even recently, moving to the East Coast wasn’t an obvious choice.

Leaving our first home.
Starting again in a new state.
New community.
New routines.

There were many late-night conversations where Kaitlyn and I
asked each other:

“Are we sure about this?”

Because when you look at someone’s life online, you usually see
the clean version of the story.

The highlights. The milestones. The house.

But you don’t see the quiet phases.

The uncertainty.

The periods where progress feels slow. Or invisible.

That’s actually the phase most international students are in.

Sharing apartments - Counting expenses - Applying to jobs (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/gkuk5de0rqf5hl9kkrxhrh8e3wm7dhmh90k6e/qvh3m828i7hdzl0rgvul/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
) - Waiting for visa results.

Trying to build a life in a country that still feels unfamiliar.

It’s not glamorous.

But it’s real.

And when I stood in the living room of this new house, the
thought that kept coming back was this:

None of this happened because of one big moment.

It was hundreds of small decisions.

Choosing the cheaper option when money was tight.

Choosing to work on something after a long day.

Choosing to keep building skills even when results were slow.

Choosing to stay patient when life didn’t move as fast as you
hoped.

The big milestones look dramatic from the outside.

But when you live through them, they’re actually built very
quietly.

One small choice at a time.

So if you’re reading this from a small apartment, a shared room,
or a late-night study session somewhere in the U.S., I just want
to say this.

​You don’t need to figure out the entire future right now. (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/gkuk5de0rqf5hl9kkrxhrh8e3wm7dhmh90k6e/qvh3m828i7hdzl0rgvul/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
)​

You don’t need to know how everything will work out.

You just need to focus on the next step that moves you forward.

One better project.

One stronger application.

One skill that makes you more valuable.

One opportunity you take seriously.

And over time, those small decisions start stacking up in ways
you can’t see yet.

I’m incredibly grateful for the journey so far.

For the people who supported me.

For everyone who has watched the videos, sent messages, or shared
kind words over the years.

I truly mean it when I say this.

You’ve played a part in this journey.

If you’re currently in the $1 taco phase of life, please keep
going.

Your future self is already walking through doors you can’t see
yet.

— Yudi J

The Monthly AI Recap

By Google


By Google

    
    
    Read this article on LinkedIn to join the conversation
Read on LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/latest-ai-news-we-announced-february-google-rmrye?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BpZc8lCh%2FQiicVFWQ4rKZ3w%3D%3D&midToken=AQEIM4HzHiyK2w&midSig=0MCH8qhi-pWI81&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-ghmp60~mmjf3mdk~67-null-null&eid=ghmp60-mmjf3mdk-67
  
Want to keep up with all the AI news coming out of Google? We've got you covered. This new monthly digest breaks down the most important updates and insights, all in one place. Hit the subscribe button to follow along! For us, February was about global impact. At the AI Impact Summit in India, we demonstrated how our ongoing breakthroughs in AI are now solving real-world challenges for people everywhere — and we launched new partnerships and investments to make sure everyone benefits. We see AI as an enabling technology that can help people achieve their goals — whether you're a researcher, entrepreneur or Olympic athlete. On the slopes, in a research lab, or right in the palm of your hand, Google's latest AI announcements are here to help you. We announced new partnerships and investments at the AI Impact Summit. As world leaders gathered in New Delhi, India, we shared how we’re partnering to make AI work for everyone. That includes new Impact Challenges to help advance science and spark innovation for governments, as well as new national partnerships in India for AI and collaborations to accelerate scalable AI solutions in science and education. CEO Sundar Pichai delivered opening remarks at the AI Impact Summit. Sundar explained why “no technology has [him] dreaming bigger than AI” and called on leaders to pursue AI boldly, approach it responsibly, and work through this moment in AI’s development together. He shared ways that Google is ensuring everyone benefits with major infrastructure investments and new AI skills training. For more on the AI Impact Summit, read reflections from Sundar and Demis Hassabis. We released Nano Banana 2, combining Pro image capabilities with Flash image speed. That means you can now access high-quality image generation with faster results across products like the Gemini app and Google Search. We’re also continuing to improve tools like SynthID to help you identify AI-generated content. Developers can now build with Nano Banana 2 and deploy sophisticated visual creation at scale with an amazing price-performance ratio. We released our most advanced music generation tools. Lyria 3 allows you to create custom music in the Gemini app. That means you can describe an idea or upload a photo or video, and Gemini will generate a 30-second track with custom cover art. On top of sharing that news, we also shared six tips to get you started prompting Lyria 3. And as an added creative tool, we also announced that ProducerAI is joining Google Labs. Whether you’re refining lyrics or a melody, ProducerAI is a music creation partner that can help turn your imagination into dynamic, comprehensive songs. We shared new ways to create images and videos in Flow. To help you generate, edit and animate images and videos in a single workspace, we’re bringing our top AI capabilities into Flow. You can create high-fidelity images and instantly use them as building blocks for video generation, all in one place. With an updated interface, it’s now even easier to search, filter, and manage your assets. We released Gemini 3.1 Pro to help tackle your most complex tasks. Gemini 3.1 Pro is a smarter, more capable baseline model for complex problem-solving, demonstrating more than double the reasoning performance of 3 Pro. It’s designed to help you when a simple answer isn’t enough, whether you’re looking for a clear, visual explanation of a topic, synthesizing data into a single view or pulling together a creative project. Gemini 3.1 Pro is available to developers, enterprises and consumers via various platforms. We released a major upgrade to Gemini 3 Deep Think. We collaborated with world-class scientists and researchers to improve Gemini 3 Deep Think. Designed specifically for the complexities of science and engineering, the updated Gemini 3 Deep Think excels where data is messy and solutions aren't black-and-white. It moves beyond abstract theory to deliver practical, actionable results for technical challenges. The new Deep Think is now available in the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers. Researchers, engineers and enterprises can express interest in early access to test Deep Think via the Gemini API. We shared our view on what’s required to achieve digital resilience in the AI era at MSC. New technologies mean new frontiers for strategic competition. We’re already seeing how threats are evolving, and how old ways of responding are failing to meet the moment. That’s why at the 62nd Munich Security Conference, Google President of Global Affairs Kent Walker called for a collaborative approach to security and outlined how partners could work together to build resilience without sacrificing control over their data. We shared how Google Cloud helped Team USA find their edge with AI. email_text:
( http://devpost.com )

We know as devs and innovators, your expertise normally lies behind the scenes, but the submission video needs time and care too! It's often the first (and sometimes only!) thing that judges review. Your video tells the story behind your project, providing a clear avenue to showcase your software and talent. 

Prep your elevator pitch and don’t forget to include:

* how your project meets the hackathon requirements
* tools you used
* problem your project addresses
* solution your project addresses

Make sure you have access to the GitLab AI Hackathon group to publish your agent. Request Access here. ( https://forms.gle/EeCH2WWUewK3eGmVA )

Demo your project in a way that shows judges how real-world users will interact and benefit from it.

* Time-saving Tip
* Write out your script and practice it before you record to ensure you cover everything in the time limit
* Pro(crastinator) Tip
* We CANNOT stress this enough: Don't wait until the last minute to upload your video! Due to file size, format, and your Internet connection, uploading a video to Facebook Video, YouTube, Vimeo, or Youku could take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours

With a powerhouse model like Amazon Nova at your fingertips, the floor is high, but the ceiling is nonexistent. To move from "cool prototype" to the winner’s circle, you need to think like a judge. We aren't just looking for code; we’re looking for a story, a solution, and a spark.

🧠 How to "Wow" the Judges
*
The Name: Give it a soul. Instead of "Nova UI Automator," try something like "GhostCursor" or "SwiftStep."
*
The "Why": Start your description with the problem. "Every day, 5,000 managers struggle with X..." Then explain why Nova was your secret sauce.
*
The Demo: Show, don’t just tell. Get to the UI/CLI within the first 30 seconds. If you're building with Nova 2 Sonic, show the user's reaction—human connection wins every time.
*
The Repo: A clean README is your resume. If we can't understand the architecture or how to run it, we can't judge it.

✅ Submission Checklist
Use this list to ensure your project isn't disqualified on a technicality:

[ ] The Core: Does your app use an Amazon Nova foundation model (Nova 2 Lite, Nova 2 Sonic, Multimodal Embedding) or the Nova Act service on AWS?

[ ] The Team: Are all teammates added and have they accepted the invitation?

Maker Mindset

By ROSHAN RAVANI


By ROSHAN RAVANI

    
    
    Read this article on LinkedIn to join the conversation
Read on LinkedIn

The Ravani Report — Issue #7 You've been here before. A workflow that runs clean. A prompt you've tested, iterated, refined. Outputs that come back fast. Everything looks like progress. Then you show it to someone — a user, a teammate, yourself at 11pm with fresh eyes — and something is off. Not broken. Not crashing. Just... wrong in a way that's harder to name. You go back and fix the prompt. It breaks differently. You fix it again. Third iteration, you're mostly there. Except now you're not even sure what "there" means anymore. Three days in, you realize: the prompt was never the problem. You built something efficient. You just aimed it at the wrong outcome from the start. What Actually Happened When an AI workflow breaks, the instinct is to look at the output and ask: what did the model do wrong? Wrong question. The right question is earlier: what did I ask it to optimize for? Most workflow failures aren't model failures. They're direction failures. The system did exactly what you told it to do. You told it to do the wrong thing. This is harder to catch than a crash. A crash stops you. A direction failure ships to users. The Real Pattern Six issues ago, this newsletter started with one idea: early signals beat crowded trends. Since then, the thread has been about learning to see clearly — designing focus, filtering noise, cutting excess. But here's the thing nobody says out loud: Clarity without direction is just faster confusion. You can have a clean system, sharp attention, and zero distractions — and still spend three weeks building something no one needs, pointed at an outcome that doesn't matter. Efficiently. That's the Issue 7 problem. Not distraction. Not chaos. Misdirection. The Framework: Direction Before Optimization Before you build the workflow, before you write the first prompt, before you pick the model — answer this: What does a good output actually do for the person receiving it? Not what it contains. What it does. Most prompts are written around content: "summarize this," "extract that," "generate 5 options." Useful prompts are written around function: "help a first-time builder decide whether to keep going in under 60 seconds," "surface the one blocker hiding in this update," "make this decision feel obvious, not complete." The difference is direction. Three questions before any AI workflow: What decision does this output enable? If the answer is vague, the prompt will be too. What does the user do immediately after reading it? If nothing — the workflow solves the wrong problem. What would make this output useless even if it's correct? Build that into the prompt as a constraint. These aren't prompt engineering tricks. They're direction checks. Run them before you write a single instruction. What This Looks Like in Practice The shift is small but it changes everything. Before: "Summarize this user feedback and group it by theme." After: "Read this user feedback and surface the one thing, if unaddressed, will cause the next user to leave. One sentence. Be specific." Same model. Same data. Completely different direction. The first prompt produces information. The second produces a decision. That's the only gap that matters. The Close The last six issues were about building the conditions to think clearly. This is where that clarity gets tested. It's easy to optimize. It takes judgment to aim correctly first. Most builders — including me, regularly — skip the direction check because it's slower than just starting. We'd rather iterate on a broken workflow than sit with an uncomfortable question about what we're actually trying to do. The fix isn't a better prompt library. It's the discipline to ask what does this need to accomplish before asking how do I build this. Efficient at the right thing. That's the target. Until Issue #8 — run experiments, not plans. — Roshan

--------------------------

This is advanced-level interviewing.

He noticed:

* When interviewer leaned in

* When they wanted shorter answers
* When they wanted deeper thinking

That only comes from volume.

When you’ve done 5 interviews, you freeze.

When you’ve done 80, your nervous system stabilizes.

That’s the difference.

-----------------------
3. Non-Desperate Energy
-----------------------

Earlier interviews?
He had no offers.
Every tough question felt fatal.

Later interviews?
He had 2 backup offers.

Mindset shifted from:
“I need this.”

To:
“I’m evaluating this too.”

That psychological shift alone improves performance.

Which is why I tell my students:
Build backup pipelines early.

Even if product is your goal,
Apply to adjacent roles.

Confidence compounds.

---------------------
4. Recruiter Leverage
---------------------

When he got 2 offers, he didn’t hide them.

He informed recruiters strategically.

Result?

* Faster interview scheduling
* Higher priority handling
* Clearer timelines

Recruiters close roles.
They need strong candidates.

If you position yourself correctly, you increase leverage.

----------------------------------------
5. The Real Myth: Brand Doesn’t Save You
----------------------------------------

He was from a top program.

Still:

* 600+ applications
* 20 interviews
* 3 offers

Brand is an amplifier.
Not a shortcut.

Strategy > school.

Always.

* Feeling mentally drained

For people who are serious and tired of guessing.

You are not competing casually anymore.

You are competing against:

* Experienced candidates

 <https://replit.com>



Thursday, March 5, 2026


The last two weeks have been busy.

We shipped Replit Pro, our biggest tier update ever, completely restructured 
how Agent modes work, and shipped the ability to create video, entirely in 
Replit.

Let's jump in!




Replit Animation



 You have to see it to believe it - you can now make full-featured animations 
using Replit withReplit Animation 
<https://docs.replit.com/replitai/animated-videos> (We used it to make the gif 
above!)

To get started, head to the prompt box mention "video" in your initial prompt 
- we'll toggle on to video mode for you or select "animation" from the dropdown 
under "App" mode.


Replit Pro


We've just launched our most powerful plan yet - Replit Pro. 
<https://replit.com/pricing>

 Pro brings an expanded set of features for our most avid builders - expanded 
credits, priority support, and exclusive community access - with even more 
features on the way


New Agent Modes



 We've added new Agent modes <https://docs.replit.com/replitai/agent-modes> to 
improve how you build - choose between Economy and Power modes to optimize cost 
& power:

Economy Mode: Optimized for cost. Uses fewer credits per task - prompts cost 
roughly a third of Agent 3, so you can send significantly more prompts for the 
same price.

Power Mode: Optimized for performance. Uses more powerful models for complex 
tasks, larger codebases, and harder problems.


📌 Other new features


 * Background memory compression - Agent no longer stops to "optimize memory," 
so you can now build faster!
 * Expanded MCP integrations - New options available with single-click setup at
replit.com/integrations <https://replit.com/integrations>
 * Skills search - Browse and install popular Skills directly without 
prompting Agent or uploading files.Check it out! 
<https://docs.replit.com/replitai/skills>
 * System theme support - Replit now follows your system preference, or 
manually toggle light/dark from the quick menu
 * Enhanced collaboration - Unlimited Workspaces, simplified sharing, and 
per-Workspace usage tracking on all paid plans
 * Deployment visibility settings - Scope app visibility within your 
organization (Teams and Enterprise)
 * Password manager keyboard navigation - Full keyboard support for logging in 
via password manager extensions

 You can find weekly updates and more in our changelog 
<https://docs.replit.com/updates>.


📹 Videos & tutorials


 I've been shipping tutorials on my channel 
<https://www.youtube.com/@mattpalmer> and the Replit YouTube 
<https://www.youtube.com/@replit>.

The HireReady Newsletter Vol. 83: Conducting Counter-Intelligence During the Post-Interview Silence

That quiet period after a great interview can be tough. It's easy to fall into a cycle of refreshing your email and overthinking every little detail. But what if, instead of passively waiting, you could actively gather intelligence that not only eases your anxiety but also prepares you for the next steps? This week, we're swapping nervous energy for proactive investigation.

Let's turn this waiting game into a winning one.

🛠️ The job search hacks 🛠️

🔍 Use the Jobscan Job Tracker to Decode Your Interview 🔍

The real magic of the Jobscan Job Tracker isn't just in tracking your applications; it's in its potential as a post-interview intelligence tool. Think of the "Notes" section as your private detective's notebook. After an interview, immediately log the specific keywords, phrases, and project names your interviewers used. Pay close attention to the language they used to describe the role, the team's challenges, and their goals. This isn't just about remembering what was said; it's about building a linguistic profile of the company's internal dialogue.

Next Steps

After your next interview, open up your Jobscan Job Tracker. In the "Notes" for that specific job, create a new entry titled "Interviewer Keywords." List out all the significant terms and phrases you remember.

Now, here's the clever part: over the next week, keep an eye on the company's other job postings. When a new one appears, even if it's not for your role, scan it for the keywords you noted. This can give you invaluable clues about the company's current priorities, internal projects, and the specific language they use to define success.

(https://info.jobscan.co/e3t/Ctc/S+113/cvzDf04/VWMGtL2pyCDjN378FLNmj4pqW99f7mw5Lgy7sN9cd5Hl3gP0xW7lCdLW6lZ3nkW100C607F37YHN4YBV4t4LyMZVwPxQs29sLyTW3KbBg96X-F_TW4qTHxT6XRk2xW5bBSMM2c8xV2W3nyCW84GyyfJW4kNYyB8QkBJjW73cFkx1z36C9W5b0wlb6nMbMKW4yb4pl6HQq5TW2QZBXZ2xHmVXW40M-Sg1GkGYFW1KQDsR6H_nNTW7sb6jZ2wRrFgN33JN1N1x9MvW1sFcH66FgFk6W75ph5w3SFtHzW47q_QH93rtKwVp40PW6Y-5XzVz8X2J6vjChkW1XVCxH13h3MbW2P-Zss3J4wDyV5_14Y1spjq9f61mvY-04 )

🕵️ Conduct Social Media Reconnaissance 🕵️

Instead of just scrolling through your interviewers' LinkedIn profiles, it's time to become a more sophisticated observer. What are they talking about right now? What articles are they sharing? What professional events are they attending or speaking at? This isn't about being nosy; it's about understanding their current professional mindset and the conversations that are top-of-mind for them and their team. This insight can be incredibly valuable if you're called back for another round of interviews, allowing you to tailor your conversation to their present-day challenges and interests.

Next Steps

Use a social media monitoring tool (there are free ones available) to set up alerts for your interviewers' names and the company's key team members. You can also do this within LinkedIn by saving searches for content by these individuals. Spend 15 minutes each day reviewing the content they are engaging with. Are they excited about a new technology? Are they grappling with a particular industry trend? This information can help you formulate more insightful follow-up questions and demonstrate a deeper level of engagement with their work.

Tool: Optimize Your LinkedIn Profile for a Better Job Search
(https://info.jobscan.co/e3t/Ctc/S+113/cvzDf04/VWMGtL2pyCDjN378FLNmj4pqW99f7mw5Lgy7sN9cd5Hl3gP0xW7lCdLW6lZ3myW1gFmy21R6XgdW6StzbY55z4mCV3cW087m12JbW88W0hl8SVLpkW6ZRvZJ5mddmgW3wXwpt7hS2WxW3pQgb_49wyCBW5Q_rSy2RcggkVZs0PR7ydTM4W92WQjl6TtfFmW1dTxGG50PrGMW8My337128ydPW2zQz617tSfxHVWJKnD6vJd9RW7yp3Yp2bb1zGW8MWyfc5YHvLxW3p-FTj7gkwzJF739QdFHJcDVrr3KD1hcMd9W3c4kk_5nmYVhW7ZMphM8qBTRBW8ylp8y8-sPZ0W6_9Pww37YrgxVHJjD75Gq7wzf7CpNLP04 )

🔗 Activate Your "Whisper Network" 🔗

Your professional network is one of your most valuable assets, especially during the post-interview silence. Now is the time to activate your "whisper network" - the trusted contacts in your field who may have connections to the company you interviewed with. The key here is subtlety and respect. You're not asking them to spy for you, but rather to provide general insights and context that can help you understand the company culture and decision-making process.

Next Steps

Search your LinkedIn connections for people who currently or previously worked at the company. If you have a trusted first-degree connection, reach out and ask if they'd be willing to share their general impressions of the company culture and the team you interviewed with. For second-degree connections, ask a mutual contact for a warm introduction. Frame your request as seeking advice and perspective, not as an attempt to get inside information on the hiring decision. A simple, "I recently interviewed for a role at [Company] and would love to get your perspective on the company culture" is a great way to start the conversation.

(https://info.jobscan.co/e3t/Ctc/S+113/cvzDf04/VWMGtL2pyCDjN378FLNmj4pqW99f7mw5Lgy7sN9cd5HF3gP0xW7Y8-PT6lZ3nCW7s3VWq3JGhqvW4gCCzT1LKBlrW6TnBPn3q-l-YVQdZnw5JlndPW71HTV480xV8mW8GhFyp2k_bsLN1Q0sS-g-MR0N7-3xvbFx7dHW15R91j1-5BG7VS5wj68yhqKCW17zCkd4-DNF6N62HTx2QWjJRW2SrdGH98BYNYW90Ljc73qXBwhN7TJK1VbqVPyW1PPT3M22xJGFVXv76R2Vdl47MMzG7nMDC6KW2k-FBq2pNcr6N58RMfmBTSRTW7BLMbf2mkXWDVSltNP1cn3hCW513Lzf8FB7LcW5ysHMS8pQxF5N3NjBQY-pRTfW11Jtqj49WJvbf4-1DQY04 )

📰 Become a Company News Analyst 📰

While you're waiting, the company you interviewed with is still operating, making announcements, and reacting to market changes. By becoming a temporary "news analyst" for the company, you can gain a deeper understanding of its current trajectory, which might give you clues about the hiring timeline. Major news, like a new product launch, a round of funding, or a significant leadership change, can all impact the speed of the hiring process.

Next Steps

Set up Google Alerts for the company's name, as well as the names of key executives. Read their latest press releases, blog posts, and watch any recent interviews with their leadership. This will not only keep you informed but also provide you with excellent material for a well-timed and intelligent follow-up email.

For example, if they announce a new product, you could send a brief note congratulating them and briefly mentioning how your skills align with this new direction. This shows you're engaged and thinking strategically about how you can contribute.

(https://info.jobscan.co/e3t/Ctc/S+113/cvzDf04/VWMGtL2pyCDjN378FLNmj4pqW99f7mw5Lgy7sN9cd5HF3gP0xW7Y8-PT6lZ3p4W3nLrHm6hfbz2MxTkYq30-xRW5wX2QV5LRlQzW75Nnqh6ht_tXW5FTfxf2N_QbpW3jv0t63rPDk4W3tRL8L38tJWNW3dnn3z86F_DFW88nG1Q9h77LDVh441r1KD2J4W4SCs0v7y5J-8N5Rdd39W4WqFW2q_bVr36bJXpW7JbJFZ64VjThW4pfTTg1CkX1LW2hBWw-3Hs5lRW8yZ4qL6QvTHRW1l5vR16_0xwcW5rJjQc32lwF3W31d11T1N3Br1W1M4gx_23j7ZwW4QfkkR7KDpbjW2HsmQt5RZg2rVLpQ7P67hqF1W17bmX_1HFlCWVhbJWV7WFgmyf3Tn3JK04 )

🧭 Chart Your "Alternative Futures" 🧭

One of the most anxiety-inducing parts of the post-interview wait is the feeling of being powerless. To counteract this, take control of the narrative by creating an "Alternative Futures" chart. This is a simple but powerful exercise where you map out your potential next steps for every possible outcome: you get the offer, you get a polite rejection, or you hear nothing at all. The goal is to have a pre-planned, proactive response for each scenario, so you're not left scrambling or feeling dejected.

Next Steps

Create a simple three-column chart. In the first column, list the possible outcomes: "Offer," "Rejection," and "Silence." In the second column, brainstorm your immediate next steps for each. For "Offer," this might include preparing your salary negotiation points. For "Rejection," it could be sending a gracious thank-you note and asking for feedback. For "Silence," it might be a plan to send a final, professional follow-up after a specific date. In the third column, write down a positive affirmation or a small reward for yourself for navigating this challenging phase of the job search. This simple act of planning can restore your sense of agency and keep you moving forward.

Article: How to Follow Up on a Job Application
(https://info.jobscan.co/e3t/Ctc/S+113/cvzDf04/VWMGtL2pyCDjN378FLNmj4pqW99f7mw5Lgy7sN9cd5HY3gP0xW8wLKSR6lZ3mnW6xmrvb4cW5j0W6mqx7G570RCMW1FD1NB5Cf0Y9VHvkcQ53TlTtW3GMXDx7BKlMGW805B6J5RKdZ2W65-_Dr4gDhbqN3mXR7ZlTVqNW4SBLCV5_9dh4W1KjT-n7qlQ0XW78QPxL3jrYslW9kt06l3mPptpW8N5NXQ5kDfF5W4Crg8d1KvRfVW18kcKg6S4CrvW81DM1M90jm_ZW7qn6116vsrGhW7vXpkN756S7vW7rXL9L41WRqcW1SdxFQ6l4J6PW1k5RHz4pSXyfW5Z1FYd86ptCWN333pjysXKvvW42mGDN83xfRcW1gGtxS4HXydtW4PQcMw6YD45zW4YzJwg6wlnRcW7N4WDs6KPbRrdrp6yF04 )

Remember, this period of waiting is not a reflection of your worth or your abilities. It's simply a part of the process. By channeling your energy into these proactive strategies, you're not just passing the time; you're actively investing in your career. You've got this. Keep your head up, stay resourceful, and know that the right opportunity is just around the corner.

As AI scales across industries, a new question is top of mind: Who truly controls your data, your models, and the infrastructure your business depends on? Our latest guide, Digital Sovereignty in the Era of AI, breaks down why this has become a top‑line priority for every organization embracing AI, detailing how sovereignty has evolved from a narrow “data‑residency issue” to a holistic business mandate covering data, models, governance, and more.  Get an overview of the insights below ⤵ Sovereignty pressure has never been higher ⚡ According to our research, organizations face mounting pressure from AI-driven regulatory requirements, escalating cyberthreats and geopolitical risk, and new national sovereignty mandates with 65% of governments expected to introduce requirements by 2028.  Here's what this means → companies can no longer rely solely on global, vendor‑operated systems. They must maintain verifiable, operational authority over critical workloads, especially those powered by AI. What digital sovereignty means today 🔍 We define modern digital sovereignty as an organization’s ability to control its data, models, IT operations, governance, and compliance posture—end‑to‑end and across jurisdictions. This goes beyond traditional compliance concerns to encompass: ✅ Who can access your AI models ✅ Where inference runs ✅ How governance is enforced ✅ Who holds the keys, logs, and administrative authority  In short → Sovereignty is now a system property, not a contract clause.  Discover the impact of digital sovereignty below ⤵ Sovereignty by design 🛡️ The guidebook introduces concepts that are now reshaping enterprise strategy, including: ✅ Customer‑operated control planes (full operational authority) ✅ In‑boundary identity and key management ✅ Local logs and telemetry for auditability ✅ Governed AI inference with traceability These capabilities allow organizations to modernize, re‑host, or expand AI workloads without ceding control to external cloud operators. 👉 Unlock the rest of the insights Tune in for more 🎧 Now available on demand, tune into "Digital Sovereignty & AI You Can Trust: IBM's Vision on the Future of Software", an IBM Technology Summit session exploring how organizations are navigating the growing demands of digital sovereignty and what it takes to deploy AI securely, compliantly, and at scale without slowing innovation. 👉 Register to watch on demand

By leveraging technically validated and secure connectors, builders can create specialized Rovo agents that act as a single control point for cross-functional work. Whether you’re investigating a metric drop in Amplitude or drafting a targeted campaign in HubSpot, these agents perform the heavy lifting—hunting, stitching, and recommending actions—so you can focus on high-level decision-making. Whether you’re an engineer aligning outdated documentation with new code or a marketer crafting on-brand copy from many sources, Think deeper bridges the gap between speed and thoroughness. Yudi here,

I have something exciting to share with you:)

FREE Study in USA Event
-----------------------

​

I’m coming to India for a Study in USA event series across 4
cities.

​

If you're planning for Fall 2026, Spring 2027, or even Fall 2027,

​

✅ Clear strategy for Fall 2026 or 2027 plans

✅ Networking and practical Q&A

​

This event is free to attend.

​

Seats are limited because I want these events to feel personal.
​

Sign up for the city you’re in and let’s make a plan that
actually works for you.

​

Here’s where I’ll be:

* Hyderabad – 14th March ➜ Register here (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/qdu3pe0r67c7h4w7664hlh8d04k0mf4hl6wzv/z2hghnhenve8r3ap/aHR0cHM6Ly9sdW1hLmNvbS9oeWQyMDI2

)​

​
Let's start with our newsletter,

Last year, one of my Accelerator students (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/qdu3pe0r67c7h4w7664hlh8d04k0mf4hl6wzv/n2hohvhvmpvk5zs6/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
)​ sent me a message in January:

“I think I messed up. I’ve applied to 150 roles. Two interviews.
Both rejected. I don’t know if I’m built for this.”

He had:

* CMU admit
* Intel on his resume
* AI background
* Strong academics

And still… zero traction.

Let me tell you what actually changed his trajectory. A system
shift.

----------------------
Phase 1: The Ego Crash
----------------------

When he landed in the U.S., he thought:

* Good university
* Good brand
* Decent experience
* PM pivot will be manageable

Reality check?

150 applications → 0 offers
3 months → no interviews
Resume revised 15 times

This is where most people spiral.

Instead, we rebuilt from scratch.

---------------------------------------------------
Phase 2: Warm Networking (Strategic, Not Desperate)
---------------------------------------------------

Before most students even land, they start applying blindly.

He did something different.

He spoke to 40+ product managers before classes even started.

Not for referrals.

For intelligence.

He asked:

* When do PM internships open?
* How many does your company hire?
* What actually matters in screening?

He learned something brutal:

Some cohorts of 200 students had only 3 PM interns.

This changed his expectations.

This is why I tell Accelerator (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/qdu3pe0r67c7h4w7664hlh8d04k0mf4hl6wzv/n2hohvhvmpvk5zs6/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
) students: If you don’t know the hiring math, you are playing
blind.

------------------------------
Phase 3: Resume Identity Shift
------------------------------

He had a pure engineering resume.

99% model accuracy.
Published GitHub models.
Technical benchmarks.

Great engineer.
Wrong positioning.

We rebuilt it through a product lens.

Instead of:
“Improved model accuracy to 99%.”

It became:
“Improved model adoption by X%, reduced manual workflow by Y
hours weekly.”

Same work.
Different framing.
Different identity.

You must become the role before you get the role.

Most students try to “transition” without transforming.

That does not work anymore.

----------------------------------------------------
Phase 4: Post-Application Networking (The Real Edge)
----------------------------------------------------

Here’s what separated him.

After applying daily, he didn’t just wait.

He:

* Applied.
* Identified recruiter.
* Identified likely hiring manager.
* Sent 3-line email:* Who he is
* What value he brings
* Clear ask: “Would appreciate if you could review my
application.”

Every day.
3–5 targeted follow-ups.
For months.

Result?

Faster rejections.
Faster responses.
Actual traction.

One short email later helped move him from software screening to
product screening at the same company.

That email changed his career.

Most of you are applying.
Few of you are activating.

------------------
The Breaking Point
------------------

In January, after final-round rejection, he had a panic attack.

Not because of visa pressure.

Because expectations collapsed.

This is the invisible part no one posts on LinkedIn.

We talked about one thing:

“You are not failing. Your strategy is incomplete.”

So we pivoted.

He started applying to ML roles again as backup.

Confidence came back.

Offers started coming.

And something interesting happened…

When desperation left, performance improved.

He eventually landed:

* 3 offers
* 20+ interviews total
* 600+ applications
* 70+ mock interviews
* 1 product role from 1000 applicants

One seat.
He took it.

------------------
The Lesson For You
------------------

Stop romanticizing:

* Referrals
* Brand names
* Luck
* Right timing

Start engineering:

* Application velocity
* Post-application activation
* Resume identity alignment
* Interview reps

​Inside the Accelerator (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/qdu3pe0r67c7h4w7664hlh8d04k0mf4hl6wzv/n2hohvhvmpvk5zs6/aHR0cHM6Ly9hY2FkZW15Lnl1ZGlqLmNvbS9qb2JodW50bmw=
), this is exactly what we build:

* Application tracking sheets
* Networking scripts
* Resume rewrites by role
* Mock interview drills
* Weekly execution accountability

Because mindset without mechanics is useless.

If you are serious about playing at this level,
You need systems, not hope.

More in the next newsletter - I’ll break down how he converted 1
seat out of 1000 applicants.

email_text:
Hi!

 

Welcome to Inngest's March product newsletter. This past month we really aimed to improve reliability, speed, and overall experience. Here's what you need to know (plus a few things we learned along the way):

The Big One:

- v4 of the TypeScript SDK ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/typescript-sdk-v4.0?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) is now in beta 🎉. Composable trigger helpers, better schemas, more intuitive middleware, checkpointing by default... and all much faster.

Check out our migration guide ( https://www.inngest.com/docs/reference/typescript/v4/migrations/v3-to-v4?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) to get started.

 What Else is New?

- Agent Skills ( https://www.inngest.com/docs/ai-dev-tools/agent-skills ) help your favorite agents work with Inngest.

- Durable endpoints ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/introducing-durable-endpoints?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) make APIs unbreakable without refactoring. 

- Checkpointing ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/introducing-checkpointing?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) unlocks near-zero latency for durable workflows.

- The Constraint API ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/announcing-the-constraint-api?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) further drives latency down and scalability up.

What's Better?

- Enhanced Traces ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/introducing-enhanced-traces ) brings more data to the front end, to make it even easier to find the source of slowdowns.

Play ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ytQdo3FwidQ )

What's Worth Reading? 

We've been building a ton with agents lately. Check out our learnings (with source code!):

- Your Agent Needs a Harness, Not a Framework ( https://x.com/djfarrelly/status/2028556984396452250?s=20&utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email ) by Dan Farrelly

- What we Learned About Building Agentic Features ( https://www.inngest.com/blog/how-we-built-insights-ai-with-inngest ) by Andy Lawrence

 

👋 That's all for now! See you back here next month.

Yudi here,

I have something exciting to share with you:)

FREE Study in USA Event
-----------------------

​

I’m coming to India for a Study in USA event series across 4
cities.

​

If you're planning for Fall 2026, Spring 2027, or even Fall 2027,
this event will help you understand:

​

✅ Clear strategy for Fall 2026 or 2027 plans
✅ Admissions, funding, and visa talk without fluff
✅ Job market and profile building tips
✅ Networking and practical Q&A

​

This event is free to attend.

​

Seats are limited because I want these events to feel personal.
​

Sign up for the city you’re in and let’s make a plan that
actually works for you.

​

Here’s where I’ll be:

* Hyderabad – 14th March ➜ Register here (
https://604b57c3.click.kit-mail3.com/r8ulr2p0neaoh3486e6c2hdnlgw33t7h365er/25h2hoh36w8mnvu3/aHR0cHM6Ly9sdW1hLmNvbS9oeWQyMDI2
